references.text: Urim and Thummim are mentioned here as part of the high priest's breastplate, which was used to seek God's will. This is the original institution of what Moses refers to in the blessing over Levi.
Moses placed Urim and Thummim in the breastplate when Aaron was consecrated as high priest, confirming the Levites' special role in administering these sacred objects.
Joshua was to stand before the priest Eleazar and seek the Lord's decision through Urim. This shows the Levites' function as mediators of God's will.
The account of Massah, where the people tested the Lord by quarreling over water. Moses refers to this event in the blessing.
The waters of Meribah where the Israelites contended with the Lord. This is the place Moses mentions in connection with the testing of Levi.
The psalm warns against hardening one's heart as at Meribah and Massah, the same places Moses mentions in the blessing over Levi.
The Levites showed their loyalty to the Lord during the golden calf incident, when they gathered to Moses and carried out judgment. This demonstrates their godliness which Moses praises.
Phinehas, a Levite, showed zeal for the Lord and received an everlasting covenant of priesthood. This illustrates the faithfulness of the Levites as 'your faithful man'.
After the exile, none of the priests could prove their lineage, and they had to wait until a priest could consult Urim and Thummim.
Malachi describes the covenant with Levi and their role as keepers of knowledge and law, which expands on Moses' blessing over the tribe.
